title: Doubled pawns: create them or avoid them?
outcomes: Decides, in unlabeled positions, whether a capture that doubles your own pawns is worth it, using what it buys and what it costs
Tells a capture the engine accepts from one it rates far worse, and a position where no pawn would be doubled
Writes down, on paper, one way to make an opponent advance his doubled pawns

steps.text: In *Doubled pawns: count what they buy* you listed what doubled pawns buy. Now you decide without labels. Before a capture that doubles your own pawns, ask what it buys (bishop pair, open file, central control) and what it costs. Rule of thumb: doubled pawns are weak when they must advance or stand alone; while they stay still they can hold. The board shows a capture the engine accepts.

steps.caption: Black to move. The capture exf4 is possible. It would leave Black with doubled pawns on f4 and f7.

line.say: exf4 doubles the pawns on f4 and f7, but no White piece can take f4, and the c- and e-files open for Black's rooks.

claims.statement: After exf4, Black's doubled pawns: f4 and f7.
After exf4, no White piece attacks f4.
After exf4 and White's best reply Bd4, the doubled pawns on f4 and f7 remain.
After exf4 the c-file and e-file are half-open for Black.
At depth 16 exf4 is the engine's best move.

steps.text: **Rule of thumb, with conditions.** Accept doubled pawns when the capture opens a file or gains the bishop pair or the centre. Avoid them when the pawns would be isolated, blocked or forced forward. To profit from the opponent's doubled pawns, a classic idea [R] is to make him advance them first; the app cannot check that, so the last step is paper. Next: one position three times, with one change each.

steps.title: Worth it, not worth it, nothing to weigh
steps.prompt: Predict which statement fits each position. In the second, Black's queen moved from b6 to a6; in the third, the White pawn on c3 is gone. Then name the one change that flipped the verdict between the first two.

Paper exercise (the app does not check it): in My games, find a position where the opponent has doubled pawns. Write the move that would make him advance one of them, and what he would give up if he did.
